subject: Model shortlist & token-mapping for onboarding: next steps
messages:
From: Sam Cho <sam.cho@blueoak.ai>
To: irene.choi@redwood.ai
Cc: elena@blueoak.ai
Date: 2028-04-02T09:12:00Z
Subject: New onboarding: model fit & token estimates

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We're moving forward with the pilot and need to lock down the model shortlist and rough token volumes so our infra and procurement teams can plan. High level:
- Primary use case: automated clinical note summarization and triage (batch + interactive via UI).
- Peak concurrent editors: ~120 (US region) with interactive rounds around 8–12 turns per session.
- Expected daily processed sessions during pilot: 3k–6k.
- Average source document length: 1,200–1,800 tokens; summaries target ~150–300 tokens.

Can you propose 2–3 model variants we should test (cost-balanced + accuracy-priority), recommended context lengths, and a rough token/day estimate for our SRE team? Attached is a quick workbook with our session assumptions (blueoak_token_profile.xlsx).

Also flag anything that would push you toward Dedicated vs Hosted for the pilot.

Thanks,
Sam
Sam Cho
Head of ML Engineering, BlueOak Analytics
From: irene.choi@redwood.ai
To: Sam Cho <sam.cho@blueoak.ai>, Elena Martinez <elena@blueoak.ai>
Cc: grace.oconnor@redwood.ai, priyom.das@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-04-03T14:06:00Z
Subject: Re: New onboarding: model fit & token estimates

Sam / Elena — thanks for the workbook and the clear usage notes. Drafting a concise shortlist + token projection below; I'll loop Jordan from Solutions for implementation notes.

Model shortlist (two lanes):
1) Accuracy-priority (one model): LLM-Large-220B-fp16 (open variant)
   - Context suggested: 4096 tokens
   - Best for high-fidelity clinical summarization, multi-turn reference retention
   - Expected avg tokens per session: source 1,400 + summary 220 + system/prompt overhead ~200 = ~1,820 tokens/session

2) Cost-balanced (two-tier approach): LLM-Medium-16B-quant + LLM-Small-7B for short runs
   - Context suggested: 2048 tokens for 16B; 1024 tokens for 7B fallback
   - Use 16B for ~80% of sessions; 7B for quick triage/low-cost endpoints
   - Expected avg tokens per session (weighted): ~1,100 tokens/session

3) Latency-optimized (if you need <500ms p95 for interactive): LLM-Tiny-2B-quant with aggressive prefix caching
   - Context: 1024 tokens (with strong KV cache)
   - Use only for the 10–15% of ultra-low-latency UI bindings

Rough daily token estimate (pilot window 3k–6k sessions/day):
- Accuracy-priority lane: 1,820 tokens/session * 3k–6k = 5.46M–10.92M tokens/day
- Cost-balanced lane (weighted): 1,100 tokens/session * 3k–6k = 3.3M–6.6M tokens/day
- Latency-optimized lane (10% of sessions): 200 tokens/session * 300–600 = 60k–120k tokens/day (small)

Recommendation: start pilot on Hosted API with the cost-balanced lane (16B primary + 7B fallback) unless you need strict data residency or guaranteed throughput — in which case Dedicated makes sense. Hosted will let us iterate on prompt templates and caching patterns quickly.

Next steps:
- Grace / Priyom: can you confirm whether the token estimates above assume prompt-engineering with one-shot examples or multi-shot templates? I kept a 200-token prompt overhead assumption.
- Sam: confirm the split of interactive vs batch and whether you expect longer multi-turn sessions for certain cohorts (e.g., clinical reviewers).

I'll prepare a short onboarding runbook (draft attached) with recommended batching, cache TTLs, and an initial rollout plan.

Best,
Irene Choi
Senior CS Manager — Redwood Inference
From: grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
To: irene.choi@redwood.ai, priyom.das@redwood.ai
Cc: jordan.blake@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-04-04T10:22:00Z
Subject: Re: New onboarding: model fit & token estimates

Irene — quick technical clarifications from infra/Optimize:
- Prompt overhead: baseline 180–240 tokens looks right given the multi-field templating described. We'll plan tests at 150 / 200 / 300 prompt sizes to measure impact.
- KV cache approach: recommend prefix-level caching for repeated patient metadata across turns (TTL 10–30 minutes). That should drop avg tokens/session by ~12–18% for interactive flows where repeated context applies.
- Batching: for nightly batch summarization, aim for large-batch runs (seq_len ~ 2k) to utilize throughput kernels on 16B quant instances. We'll provide target batch size recommendations in the runbook.
- Model routing policy: priority route to 16B (cost-balanced) with fallback to 7B; use Dedicated only if p95 latency on Hosted exceeds SLA > 800ms under peak or if token encryption-at-rest constraints require private deployment.

I've attached preliminary perf knobs and a sample load test script (inline reference). Priyom, can you convert this into the runbook appendix and produce a first-draft throughput table for 16B/7B at 1k/3k/6k sessions?

Thanks — Grace
Grace O'Connor
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood_perf_knobs.md (referenced)
From: irene.choi@redwood.ai
To: Sam Cho <sam.cho@blueoak.ai>, Elena Martinez <elena@blueoak.ai>
Cc: grace.oconnor@redwood.ai, priyom.das@redwood.ai, jordan.blake@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-04-05T16:38:00Z
Subject: Re: New onboarding: model fit & token estimates — pilot proposal & artifacts

Sam / Elena — following up with a succinct pilot proposal and artifacts attached. TL;DR:
- Pilot config (recommended): 16B-quant primary (context 2048), 7B-quant fallback (context 1024).
- Estimated daily tokens (3k–6k sessions): 3.3M–6.6M tokens/day under cost-balanced lane; we will instrument to target a 12–18% token saving via prefix KV caching during interactive flows.
- Hosted API is fine to start; switch to Dedicated if we see p95 latency > 800ms under peak or if procurement requires a dedicated contract.

Attachments included: blueoak_token_profile.xlsx (your workbook), redwood_onboarding_runbook_v1.pdf (pilot knobs, batch sizing table, rollout checklist).

Action items assigned:
- Sam: confirm the interactive vs batch split and any cohort differences by 2028-04-09.
- BlueOak SRE: share network whitelist IPs and expected peak concurrency window for us to run a smoke load test.
- Jordan: schedule a 60min technical kickoff next week to walk through the runbook and test plan.

If that all looks good we'll schedule the kickoff and kick off the load test.

Thanks — looking forward to partnering on this pilot.

Best,
Irene Choi
Senior CS Manager — Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood_onboarding_runbook_v1.pdf, blueoak_token_profile.xlsx
